newsitem.title: UK: Formula One ad breaks did not break code - watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Formula One ad breaks did not break code - watchdog.

text.p: Viewers complained about the number of commercial breaks during a British television broadcast of Formula One motor racing, but a watchdog group said on Wednesday the commercials did not break television guidelines.
The Independent Television Commission (ITC), in its latest monthly report, said 82 viewers objected to the inclusion of advertising breaks or to the number and frequency of the commercials.

ITV, Britain's leading commercial television network, broadcast the Formula One Grand Prix, choosing to air five two-minute commercial breaks during the race. Formula One had previously been broadcast by the state-operated BBC, which does not allow advertising.

Some complainants said the broadcast of soccer matches in Britain cannot be interrupted by commercials during actual play, and Formula One broadcasts should follow that example, but the ITC said the differences between the sports made the Formula One ad breaks acceptable.

"Football is focused entirely on the location of the ball," the ITC said in its report. "Formula One racing, on the other hand, is a diverse event of many foci, and so it is not possible to guarantee that all or even the most significant action will be on screen in real time."

Separately, the ITC said it had decided not to uphold complaints against ads for Tango Lemon, which included scenes of a young man at a newsagents reading a magazine called "Biggies", a couple interupted during a passionate embrace on a bed, and a dog apparently mounting a woman's leg. The ITC said restrictions already in place to limit viewing of the ads by children were adequate.

The ITC also choose not to uphold complaints against an ad for People Newspaper, which complainants said was pornographic or too sexually explicit. The ad promoted "In the People ... Forbidden French Sex secrets by Dr Vernon Coleman" and was set in a laboratory. The ad showed a woman in a white lab coat taking a bite from a banana offered her by a man similarly attired.
